ev.q: Prevalence of MBDDs was higher in each consecutive decreasing income level compared with the highest level
Parent-reported data from 2016 showed that a higher percentage of children in lower-income households had ever received a diagnosis
Overall, 17.4% of children aged 2–8 years had at least one MBDD
compared with children without MBDDs, those with MBDDs more often lived in the lowest income category (<100% of FPL; PR = 1.4)
Among children who did not see a health care provider in the past year and had a diagnosed MBDD, 81.7% received public assistance.
NSCH is a national, cross-sectional, web-based and paper-based survey

methods_quotes.q: weighted prevalence estimates, prevalence ratios (PRs), 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and Wald chi-square tests
were compared by whether their families received public assistance
Statistical software was used to account for the complex survey design.
p-value for weighted Wald chi-square test.
